memory_candidates.content: When waiting on a local long-running Bash command from inside an agent dispatch, the Bash tool's own `timeout` parameter defaults to 120000ms and auto-backgrounds the call at 120s regardless of an inner `timeout N` shell wrapper. To actually poll a long command (deploy scripts, full test suites) without stranding the turn: start it with `nohup cmd >log 2>&1 & disown; echo $! > pidfile` in ONE foreground call that captures the real PID immediately, then poll with `timeout N bash -c 'while kill -0 "$1" 2>/dev/null; do sleep 10; done' _ "$pid"` in subsequent calls. Never retry a nested-timeout background attempt without first confirming the prior attempt's PID is dead -- two concurrent instances writing to the same log file (each truncating with `>`) corrupts progress tracking.

On a heavily loaded host running many concurrent orchestrated dispatches, each independently invoking verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh, the repo's documented ~2.8-minute full gate-set baseline can stretch to 9-10 minutes purely from CPU contention -- not a hang. Before concluding a long-running local gate is stuck, check /proc for other live verify-deploy.sh/run-all.sh process trees (never via pgrep/ps|grep matched against your own waiter, which self-matches; iterate /proc/[0-9]*/cmdline directly) to distinguish contention from an actual stall.
